posts.title: Label-efficient 3D forest mapping: Self-supervised and transfer learning for instance segmentation, semantic segmentation, and species classification
posts.excerpt: We developed a label-efficient deep learning framework for 3D forest mapping, using self-supervised and transfer learning to improve individual tree segmentation and species classification from laser scanning point clouds

paper.title: Label-efficient 3D forest mapping: Self-supervised and transfer learning for instance segmentation, semantic segmentation, and species classification

posts.body:
Mapping individual trees for precision forestry, biodiversity, and carbon assessment requires detailed 3D structural and species information, typically derived from laser scanning point clouds. While deep learning offers advanced capabilities for segmenting and classifying trees, it demands extensive, labour-intensive annotated training data. To address this, we explored self-supervised and transfer learning strategies to significantly reduce the need for large datasets.

Our label-efficient approach improved performance across instance segmentation, semantic segmentation, and tree classification tasks. For instance, combining self-supervised learning with domain adaptation enhanced instance segmentation AP50 by 16.98%, and hierarchical transfer learning boosted tree classification mean Jaccard by 6.07%. This unified, open-source framework streamlines the extraction of individual tree information from point clouds, also reducing energy consumption and carbon emissions by 21%.

Full article: [Remote Sensing of Environment](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.rse.2026.115564)

posts.title: Monitoring mining impacts using harmonic decomposition of time series vegetation indices
posts.excerpt: We developed a new method, Seasonal Harmonic Anomaly Break Analysis (SHABA), to monitor and quantify vegetation changes caused by mining operations using time series vegetation indices

paper.title: Monitoring mining impacts using harmonic decomposition of time series vegetation indices
paper.journal: ISPRS Journal of Photogrammetry and Remote Sensing

posts.body:
Global mining operations cause significant vegetation disturbance, but their cumulative impact over time is often difficult to quantify remotely. We developed Seasonal Harmonic Anomaly Break Analysis (SHABA), a new breakpoint detection approach, to integrate vegetation index time series and identify both abrupt and subtle vegetation changes associated with mining activities.

We demonstrated the potential of SHABA by applying it to six geographically distributed mine sites: Cardinal River, Roșia Poieni, Trident, Carajás, Vametco, and Worsley. The resulting breakpoints accurately quantify cumulative changes associated with mine expansion and rehabilitation efforts, and indicate where secondary changes in surrounding areas might occur.

We found varied and complex mine footprint trajectories, with primary footprints showing both stepwise vegetation clearing and early regrowth consistent with rehabilitation. Secondary changes outside the direct mine footprint varied widely but were temporally correlated with mine expansion. We suggest the SHABA workflow could provide a robust approach for automated, global-scale quantification of changes in mine footprint over time, improving environmental accounting and stakeholder dialogue.

Full article: [ISPRS Journal of Photogrammetry and Remote Sensing](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.isprsjprs.2026.07.001)

posts.title: Predicting Mineralogy with Hyperspectral Data: A Benchmark Dataset and Machine Learning Framework to Enable Hyperspectral Geometallurgy
posts.excerpt: We developed and benchmarked workflows combining scanning electron microscope mineral maps with multimodal hyperspectral imaging data to predict mineralogy across entire drillcores using supervised machine learning

paper.title: Predicting Mineralogy with Hyperspectral Data: A Benchmark Dataset and Machine Learning Framework to Enable Hyperspectral Geometallurgy

posts.body:
Mineralogical data from drillcores are crucial for resource estimation and geometallurgical modelling, but hyperspectral imaging struggles with accurate quantification without extensive calibration. We built on previous work to combine scanning electron microscope (SEM) mineral maps with large-extent multimodal hyperspectral imaging data. Our goal was to relate hyperspectral features to mineral abundances using supervised machine learning models, then apply these models to infer mineralogy across entire drillcores.

We adapted the learning process for the unbalanced composition of most rocks, achieving reasonable accuracy for common rock-forming minerals. However, prediction accuracy strongly depended on training data representativity, often failing for rare and accessory minerals. We suggest robust, adaptive sampling approaches to address this, and emphasise that upscaled predictions must always be validated. Once validated, these predictions can provide crucial quantitative data, bridging the scale gap between petrographic observations, metallurgical tests, and geometallurgical models.

Paper: [https://doi.org/10.3390/min16070674](https://doi.org/10.3390/min16070674)

posts.title: Curlew 1.0: Spatio-temporal implicit geological modelling with neural fields in python
posts.excerpt: We introduce Curlew, an open-source Python package that uses neural fields for spatio-temporal implicit geological modelling

paper.title: Curlew 1.0: Spatio-temporal implicit geological modelling with neural fields in python

posts.body:
We developed Curlew, an open-source Python package for structural geological modelling using neural fields. This framework incorporates various local constraints and tailored global loss functions to ensure data-consistent and geologically realistic predictions. Random Fourier Feature (RFF) encodings are used to improve model convergence and facilitate stochastic uncertainty quantification, while also helping to learn naturally periodic features such as folds.

Curlew allows incremental construction of complex geological models through temporally-linked neural fields, each representing a specific deposition, intrusion or faulting event. Significantly, this framework allows semi-supervised learning to integrate diverse unlabelled datasets, reducing interpretation bias and potentially improving model robustness. We demonstrate these capabilities using synthetic examples and real data from a faulted stratigraphic digital outcrop model from Newcastle, Australia.

Full article: [Geoscientific Model Development](https://doi.org/10.5194/gmd-19-3455-2026)

posts.title: Hyperspectral mapping of density, porosity, stiffness, and strength in hydrothermally altered volcanic rocks
posts.excerpt: We developed machine learning models that predict density, porosity, stiffness, and strength of volcanic rocks from their hyperspectral fingerprints, offering an efficient method for characterising large areas

paper.title: Hyperspectral mapping of density, porosity, stiffness, and strength in hydrothermally altered volcanic rocks

posts.body:
Volcanic rock masses are difficult to characterise due to their heterogeneous structures and the complex interplay of volcanic, hydrothermal, and geomorphological processes. We expanded on previous research by acquiring a unique dataset of visible-near (VNIR), shortwave (SWIR), midwave (MWIR), and longwave (LWIR) infrared reflectance from samples across eight basaltic to andesitic volcanoes.

We then trained several machine learning models to predict density, porosity, uniaxial compressive strength (UCS), and Young's modulus (E) from these spectral data. Non-linear models, particularly multilayer perceptrons (MLP), explained up to 80% of the variance in density and porosity, and 65–70% in UCS and E. Explainable AI analysis showed that VNIR-SWIR absorptions, attributable to hydrothermal alteration, and MWIR-LWIR features, sensitive to volcanic glass content and fabric, were the dominant contributors.

These results demonstrate that hyperspectral imaging can serve as a robust proxy for rock physical and mechanical properties, offering an efficient and scalable method for characterising large areas of exposed volcanic rock. Integrating these data with geomechanical models could significantly enhance hazard assessment, infrastructure development, and resource utilisation in volcanic regions.

Paper: [Solid Earth](https://doi.org/10.5194/se-16-1249-2025)

posts.title: Tensorweave 1.0: interpolating geophysical tensor fields with spatial neural networks
posts.excerpt: We developed Tensorweave 1.0, a physics-informed spatial neural network designed to accurately interpolate geophysical tensor fields, even from sparse or irregularly sampled data

paper.title: Tensorweave 1.0: interpolating geophysical tensor fields with spatial neural networks

posts.body:
Geophysical tensor fields offer powerful insights into subsurface structures, but interpolating sparse or irregularly sampled measurements, such as full-tensor potential field gradiometry, is challenging. With colleagues, we developed Tensorweave 1.0, a physics-informed spatial neural network to address this.

Our method treats tensors as derivatives of an underlying scalar field, enabling consistent, high-fidelity interpolation across the entire domain. By leveraging the differentiable nature of neural networks, Tensorweave 1.0 not only honours the physical constraints of potential fields but also reconstructs the scalar and vector fields that generate the observed tensors.

We demonstrated the approach on synthetic gravity gradiometry data and real full-tensor magnetic data from Geyer, Germany. Results showed significant improvements in interpolation accuracy, structural continuity, and uncertainty quantification compared to conventional methods.

Paper: [https://doi.org/10.5194/gmd-18-7951-2025](https://doi.org/10.5194/gmd-18-7951-2025)

posts.title: Maximising the value of hyperspectral drill core scanning through real-time processing and analysis
posts.excerpt: Open-source real-time processing and analysis of hyperspectral drill-core data with crunchy and hycore.

paper.title: Maximising the value of hyperspectral drill core scanning through real-time processing and analysis

posts.body:
Check out our new paper on hyperspectral drillcore scanning. We present an open-source workflow for real-time processing and analysis of hyperspectral data, with a specific focus on mineral exploration through drill-core scanning.

Current hyperspectral drillcore analysis methods typically involve a significant delay between data acquisition and analysis, which limits the value of these rich datasets in time-critical exploration decisions. To help address this, we have developed two software frameworks, **crunchy** and **hycore**. Crunchy facilitates real-time preprocessing, correction, and analysis of hyperspectral data, while hycore manages and stores the data in a consistent structure, enabling interactive visualisation, analysis, and mosaicing.

We demonstrate the framework using data from several sediment-hosted base-metal deposits. The real-time results enabled rapid identification of key minerals and informed sampling strategies. We conclude that such real-time data could greatly inform geological logging and help ensure maximum information is extracted from valuable drillcores, in a reproducible and objective way.

Read the full article: [Frontiers in Earth Science](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/earth-science/articles/10.3389/feart.2024.1433662/full)

A team of researchers from Helmholtz-Zentrum Dresden-Rossendorf has introduced a concept for autonomous aerial systems in the paper *Intelligent Swarm: Concept, Design and Validation of Self-Organized UAVs Based on Leader–Followers Paradigm for Autonomous Mission Planning*.

The study proposes a framework for organising UAV swarms through a central leader drone that guides follower drones. The approach is intended to improve coordination, situational adaptability, and robustness of the group under changing mission requirements.

The work was a collaboration between HZDR-CASUS and HZDR-HIF, with contributions from Richard Gloaguen, Sandra Lorenz, Thomas D. Kühne, Wilfried Hamilton, Junaidh Shaik Fareedh, Aastha Singh and Yuleika Madriz Diaz.

posts.title: Integrated ROS development environment for UAV swarm programming
posts.excerpt: A Catkin-based IDE concept for building, simulating and deploying ROS/ROS2 UAV swarm software.
posts.body:
If you are developing UAV swarms with ROS/ROS2 and Catkin, you need an efficient setup to streamline the process. This proposed IDE is meant to keep tightly knit components and development utilities in one place: simulating, compiling, testing, debugging and deployment on the swarm.

The kernel is based on the Catkin build system. It combines CMake macros with Python scripts to build ROS packages, and is configured to integrate the drivers and dependencies (gazebo-ros-pkgs, mavros and mavlink) needed for communication and mission execution both in Gazebo and on the aircraft. Compared with a traditional rosbuild workflow it aims to provide:

1. automatic package detection and distribution, and the ability to build multiple interdependent apps in tandem
2. cross-compilation so generated programs can run on various drone types

The AutoTarget repository collects this work: [github.com/hifexplo/autotarget](https://github.com/hifexplo/autotarget)

posts.title: An easy explanation of 3D point clouds and applications
posts.excerpt: What point clouds are, how they differ from LiDAR, and where they are used.
posts.body:
A short FAQ on 3D point clouds: they store XYZ coordinates and often RGB (sometimes called “4D”). Advantages include precision, speed of acquisition, and straightforward visualisation.

LiDAR measures geometry; photogrammetric point clouds usually add colour. Classification assigns semantic labels to regions, while segmentation isolates individual objects — the city versus the buildings. Applications include mapping, disaster risk, urban mobility, forest management, intelligent transport and DEM generation.

posts.title: Spectral Characterization of Battery Components from Li-Ion Battery Recycling Processes
posts.excerpt: Optical sensors for non-contact detection of Li-ion battery components in recycling streams.

paper.title: Spectral Characterization of Battery Components from Li-Ion Battery Recycling Processes

posts.body:
Excited to share a new paper on spectral characterisation of battery components from Li-ion battery recycling processes, led by Julia Richter. The work was a collaboration between TU Bergakademie Freiberg and the Helmholtz Institute Freiberg within the BMBF-funded project DIGISORT.

Addressing the need for efficient recycling strategies amid rising demand for Li-ion batteries, the study uses optical sensors for non-contact, real-time monitoring of battery-component detection. Investigating millimetre-scale particles from end-of-life batteries with five reflectance sensors, we identified the visible to near-infrared range (400–1000 nm) as optimal for discriminating aluminium, copper and other battery components, and we provide practical recommendations for industry.

Full article: [Metals 14(2):147](https://www.mdpi.com/2075-4701/14/2/147)

posts.title: Underground hyperspectral outcrop scanning for automated mine‐face mapping: The lithium deposit of Zinnwald/Cínovec
posts.excerpt: A workflow for hyperspectral geological mapping in an underground mine, validated with LIBS.

paper.title: Underground hyperspectral outcrop scanning for automated mine‐face mapping: The lithium deposit of Zinnwald/Cínovec

posts.body:
In this study we propose a workflow for using hyperspectral imaging for geological mapping in underground mining. We evaluated sensors and lighting set-ups in the laboratory and acquired data in a German underground mine. The corrected data were used to map mineral abundance and estimate Li content, validated with laser-induced breakdown spectroscopy.

Despite the challenges of underground illumination and geometry, the work aims to establish hyperspectral sensors in the extractive industry — to increase raw-material supply, advance digitalisation, and reduce environmental impact and mining risk.

Paper: [The Photogrammetric Record](https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1111/phor.12457)

posts.title: Towards a generalised processing of hyperspectral data — part 1
posts.excerpt: Masking hyperspectral cubes with SAM and Grounding DINO so only regions of interest remain.

paper.title: Towards a generalised processing of hyperspectral data — part 1

posts.body:
## Masking hyperspectral imaging data with pretrained models

By Elias Arbash. Preprint: [arXiv:2311.03053](https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.03053)

In hyperspectral data cubes, undesired background associated with noise and unknown spectral characteristics degrades subsequent processing. Masking out unwanted regions is key: processing only regions of interest improves compute cost, memory and performance.

The proposed pipeline generates a region-of-interest mask, then applies hyperspectral processing only on the masked cube. The novelty is the segmentation step. By deploying the Segment Anything model (SAM) with Grounding DINO, followed by intersection and exclusion filtering, undesired areas are removed without retraining or fine-tuning.

On a drill-core scan the method reached precision 0.97, recall 0.98 and F1 0.97 against a hand-made ground truth, and reduced the cube from 727,000 vectors to 280,584.

Please cite Arbash et al. (2023), *Masking Hyperspectral Imaging Data with Pretrained Models*, arXiv:2311.03053.

posts.excerpt: UAS magnetics and multispectral mapping of the Asuk Member for Ni–Cu–Co–PGE–Au targeting.

paper.title: Drone-based magnetic and multispectral surveys at Disko, Greenland

posts.body: Mineral exploration in the West Greenland flood-basalt province is attractive because of its resemblance to magmatic sulphide-rich systems. At Qullissat on northern Disko we combined UAS magnetics and multispectral data to build a 3-D magnetisation-vector model that includes remanence acquired during a reversal, and to account for landslide-rotated blocks when targeting Ni–Cu–Co–PGE–Au.

posts.title: Locating skarns with magnetic survey data, Geyer, Erzgebirge
posts.excerpt: Optimising ground, drone and airborne magnetic surveys for thin dipping skarns.

paper.title: Locating skarns with magnetic survey data, Geyer, Erzgebirge

posts.body: Magnetic data can be acquired from ground, drone or helicopter platforms with a variety of sensors. This study optimises survey parameters for thin, dipping skarns at Geyer in the Erzgebirge, using petrophysics and Variscan remanence. Ground and low drone surveys outperform aircraft SQUID FTMG for these targets.

posts.title: Machine learning for more responsible sourcing of critical raw materials
posts.excerpt: A review of ML for imaging sensors across exploration and mining platforms.

paper.title: Machine learning for more responsible sourcing of critical raw materials

posts.body: Digitisation and automation of the raw-material sector are required to meet Paris Agreement targets. This review covers machine learning for imaging sensors: platforms, corrections, workflows and open resources, including a geology map of Corta Atalaya derived from a random forest on a hypercloud.

posts.title: Integrated test sites for innovation ecosystems
posts.excerpt: What multi-industrial test sites need, and what they return to regional innovation systems.

paper.title: Integrated test sites for innovation ecosystems

posts.body:
Natural test sites are resource-intensive and often limited to single industries or technologies. This note draws on two strands of research to describe environment, logistics and technology requirements for multi-industrial test sites, their value for developers, and regional absorptive capacity.

paper.title: Automated Multi-Scale and Multivariate Geological Logging from Drill-Core Hyperspectral Data

posts.body: Automated multi-scale and multivariate geological logging from drill-core hyperspectral data, demonstrating how spectral products can support objective, reproducible core logging.

posts.title: Three-Dimensional, Km-Scale Hyperspectral Data of Well-Exposed Zn–Pb Mineralization at Black Angel Mountain, Greenland
posts.excerpt: Open km-scale hyperspectral data of Zn–Pb mineralisation at Black Angel Mountain, Greenland.

paper.title: Three-Dimensional, Km-Scale Hyperspectral Data of Well-Exposed Zn–Pb Mineralization at Black Angel Mountain, Greenland

posts.body:
Hyperspectral imaging is an innovative technology for non-invasive mapping, with increasing applications in many sectors. This data paper releases three-dimensional, kilometre-scale hyperspectral observations of well-exposed Zn–Pb mineralisation at Black Angel Mountain, Greenland, plus a tutorial.

The figures show (a) a true-colour RGB photogrammetric point cloud, (b) a false-colour iron index (red = Fe³⁺, green = Fe²⁺, blue = FeOH), and (c) a minimum-wavelength map for carbonate.

paper.journal: IEEE Journal of Selected Topics in Applied Earth Observations and Remote Sensing

posts.body: MS²A-Net is a multiscale spectral–spatial association network for unsupervised clustering of hyperspectral images, with applications to geological, rural and urban mapping.

posts.title: UnDIP: hyperspectral unmixing using a deep image prior
posts.excerpt: SiVM endmembers plus a CNN deep-image-prior for abundances.

paper.title: UnDIP: hyperspectral unmixing using a deep image prior

posts.body:
A deep-learning technique for linear hyperspectral unmixing: simplex-volume maximisation (SiVM) estimates endmembers, and a convolutional deep-image-prior estimates abundances. Tests span SNR 20–50 dB in Python 3.8 / PyTorch.

people.title: Richard Gloaguen

people.title: Sandra Lorenz
people.body:

- innovative exploration technologies and optical remote sensing
- digital processing of multi-modal image and point-cloud data

people.title: Gopi Krishnan Regulan
people.body: Gopi is a Robotics Research Engineer specialising in industrial robotics, mobile robotics and autonomous systems. people.title: Margret Fuchs
people.body: Margret Fuchs studied geography at the Technical University Dresden, Germany, and received her Ph.D. degree in geology at the TU Bergakademie Freiberg, Germany, in 2014. Her scientific background lies in the field of earth sciences and geochronology for understanding timing and rates of landscape evolution. The immense potential for material characterisation motivated her for innovating spectroscopy-based technologies in order to increase efficiency and accuracy in non-invasive exploration. She works in particular on the development of laser-induced fluorescence for applications in the raw material sector, adapting optical spectroscopy for material stream characterisation and on integrating multiple sensors into smart networks.

people.title: Sam Thiele
people.body: I am a structural geologist and data scientist interested in unravelling the complex systems and processes that shape volcanic and mineral systems. These are highly structured in many ways, unstructured in others, and largely hidden from view. I aim to make geoscience digital, applying data science and computer simulation to capture, synthesise and analyse diverse and multi-scale earth system data. This includes the use of cutting-edge lab, ground and drone-borne hyperspectral sensors to accurately quantify and map geological systems.

people.title: Ahmed J. Afifi

people.title: Yuleika Madriz

She received her M.Sc. degree in Sustainable Mining and Remediation Management from TU Bergakademie Freiberg, Germany. people.title: Pedram Ghamisi

people.title: Elias Arbash

research.title: Multisensor integration
research.subtitle: Real-time resource characterisation
research.body:
Optical sensors have become key to most on- and in-line scanning applications in material characterisation, digitalisation, and monitoring. They offer non-invasive sensing to identify the composition of primary and secondary materials without time- and cost-consuming sample preparation and chemical analyses. Based on material-specific physical properties, such sensors provide huge advantages for a selected material group, but show limitations for materials beyond that group, as well as for complex or unknown, variable material streams.

To innovate available technology, overcome limitations of individual sensors and expand the range of detectable materials, we focus on (1) the development of new, tailored sensor solutions and on (2) the integration of sensors into smart and agile networks. In particular, we combine reflectance hyperspectral imaging (HSI) sensors from VNIR to LWIR with emission spectroscopy using laser-induced fluorescence (LiF) to map material types and their abundances. We investigate further integration concepts for refining position information in 3D (RGB, laser profiler) for improved signal acquisition. We evaluate how resulting data can enable efficient control mechanisms and guide subsequent sensors in automated analysis cycles for validation and updating mapping results. Developed concepts then allow the toolkit of sensors (for example Raman, XRF or LIBS) to expand within the network according to the scope of individual research questions and application cases.

## Research focus

The HELIOS lab is a research infrastructure to explore the potentials and limits of optical sensors for raw material identification. The concept of HELIOS represents a combination of the EYES with the BRAIN. The EYES are our sensors to record selected physical parameters and the BRAIN provides an efficient and learning data processing architecture. Developments provide technical concepts for operational conditions and workflows for real-time data processing as a basis for process control and monitoring.

- Sensor development and integration for innovative concepts in material-stream characterisation and digitalisation in real time
- Laser-induced fluorescence (LiF) line-scan sensor integrated with HSI (inSPECtor) for drill cores
- Raman sensor for point validation integrated within HSI and LiF networks (RAMSES-4-CE)
- In-line spectroscopy-based sensor networks for HSI, LiF, Raman, XRF and LIBS
- Infrastructure for battery recycling (XRF, LIBS, robots, conveyor, GPU; InfraDatRec)
- High-performance computing (GPU, CirculAIre)

**Primary raw materials**, especially critical raw materials in drill cores and re-mining material, including rare-earth elements (inSPECtor, RAMSES-4-CE).

**Secondary raw materials**, especially complex, variable waste streams:

- automated material detection in e-waste recycling (RAMSES-4-CE)
- battery recycling (DIGISORT, RegioREC, RESTORE)
- electrolyser recycling (AI4H2 / ReNaRe / H2Giga)
- automotive recycling (Car2Car, KOLLEKT)
- additives in polymer recycling (FINEST)

## Research infrastructure

Multi-sensor work started with HELIOS mini in 2018 (RGB, HSI and LiF covering VNIR, SWIR and MWIR). Activities expanded in 2023 with robots, a laser profiler, Raman, XRF and LIBS in the circular HELIOS+ setup. LUNA lab provides further luminescence spectroscopy for dosimetric and geoscientific method development.

![Cover](fig-01.png)

research.title: Mineral mapping
research.subtitle: Rapid analysis of drill-core and geological samples
research.body:
We use various imaging sensors to acquire hyperspectral data over rock samples and drill-cores. These sensors cover the visible and near infrared (VNIR), short-wave infrared (SWIR), mid-wave infrared (MWIR) and long-wave infrared (LWIR) ranges of the electromagnetic spectrum. Various minerals show characteristic spectral features in different parts of the spectrum, so combining these datasets can provide a wealth of information on sample mineralogy.

We use both expert-rule systems based on the interpretation of spectra and machine-learning methods to map minerals rapidly. We have developed Python-based toolboxes for this purpose. By identifying and mapping minerals quickly, we can target areas with high potential for specific mineralisation.

research.title: Pointcloud processing
research.subtitle: Machine learning and 3D hyperspectral mapping
research.body:
Point clouds provide a simple but flexible way of storing, processing and visualising 3D data. Attributes from various sensors (for example geophysics or hyperspectral imaging) can be attached to 3-D points to derive spatially varying scalar fields.

Unlike image data, 3-D point clouds have an ill-defined topology — they can be treated as an unordered set — which makes many modern deep-learning techniques a significant challenge. We aim to mitigate some of these challenges by developing fit-for-purpose deep-learning methods that are compatible with high-dimensional data distributed across arbitrarily complex 3-D point clouds.

research.title: Autonomous platforms
research.subtitle: Autonomous platforms for enhanced mapping
research.body:
Autonomous platforms allow us to deploy innovative sensor technology in otherwise inaccessible regions. Unmanned aerial vehicles support high-resolution mapping of remote exploration areas, steep cliffs, or active open-pit mines. Terrestrial robots help explore confined or hazardous spaces such as underground mines and tunnels.

As part of our mission to operationalise non-invasive material mapping, we combine autonomous platforms with Earth observation technology. That means addressing technical compatibility of hyperspectral and geophysical payloads, data quality under complex conditions, and rapid processing of large datasets. We also research collaborative data collection by task-distributed drone swarms, adapted sensor design, autonomous validation, real-time hypercloud processing, and navigation that uses hyperspectral information.

## Research focus

**Innovative drone platforms.** For flexibility and interoperability with different payloads, we design, manufacture and program drone platforms in our in-house DroneLab. Payloads include hyperspectral cameras in the visible, near- and shortwave infrared, thermal cameras, magnetometers, radiometers and lidar. We also develop novel airframes and share some systems as open hardware.

**Processing workflows for innovative sensors.** Custom payloads challenge the availability of reliable geometric and radiometric correction. We contribute open tools including MEPHySTo (frame-based hyperspectral), hylite (pushbroom hyperspectral, nadir and oblique), and the MAGNETO toolbox (magnetic and radiometric data), and we integrate surface spectroscopy with subsurface geophysics (Mulsedro, MOSMIN).

**Multiscale mapping.** Drone data bridges satellite or airborne remote sensing (pixels of several to tens of metres) and sparse but detailed ground observations. Through HyperUAV we study scale effects on spectral derivatives, compare sensors and platforms, and develop super-resolution and generative enhancement — with applications to critical-raw-material exploration (for example REE-bearing carbonatites) and mine-site monitoring (MOSMIN).

**Autonomous acquisition.** AutoTarget develops a task-distributed drone network that combines long-endurance light systems with heavy-duty sensor platforms. In parallel we are autonomising mapping routines for shafts and tunnels: the terrestrial robot platform REX carries a hyperspectral camera and laser scanner, and the first underground recordings have been demonstrated.

![Cover](fig-01.png)

![Figure 1](fig-02.png)

research.title: Outcrop mapping
research.subtitle: 3D hyperspectral mapping of complex outcrops and mine faces
research.body:
Outcrop mapping provides crucial geological information in the exploration, evaluation, mining and monitoring phases of mineral-resource development. It is also an essential part of quality and process control and geotechnical risk assessment. Traditionally, geologists map visually and in direct contact with the outcrop. That is time-consuming, inefficient and subjective, and it can be dangerous: recently blasted faces are often unstable.

Remote mapping of mine walls has therefore focused on two data types: (i) detailed three-dimensional outcrop models and (ii) two-dimensional hyperspectral images from which material composition can be derived. Our work merges high-resolution point clouds with hyperspectral images into *hyperclouds*. These datasets allow integrated representation, analysis and interpretation of geometric and spectral features.

research.title: Learning
research.subtitle: Machine learning for remote sensing data
research.body: Machine-learning methods are revolutionising the analysis of remote-sensing data by enabling rapid and accurate extraction of information from large datasets. These methods improve the efficiency of tasks that inform decisions in environmental conservation, urban planning, disaster management, mineral exploration and mine monitoring.

research.title: Geological modelling
research.subtitle: Neural-field models that update with new mine and outcrop data
research.body:
Geological models have to honour sparse, mixed observations — contacts, orientations, borehole intervals, mine-face maps — and a history of folding, faulting, unconformities and intrusion. We treat that history as a graph of events whose geometry is carried by implicit fields, so structures can be built in geological order and updated when new data arrive.

**curlew** implements this as differentiable neural and analytical fields in Python. The same framework interpolates real constraints or replaces the fields with simple functions to synthesise geology for testing and inversion. **DigIT** takes those ideas into near-mine exploration: self-updating common-earth models that absorb hyperspectral mine-face maps, coupled with physical-chemical simulation of ore-forming processes so that new exposures feed deposit-scale targets rather than being lost to production.

The aim is models that stay current with mapping, remain reusable across software, and support targeting next to active and historic mines.

research.title: Remote monitoring
research.subtitle: Earth observation and in situ sensing of operating mines
research.body:
Operating mines continually change: pit walls and tailings move, surfaces weather, and new material is exposed or stored. Capturing those changes at site scale needs more than occasional surveys. We combine satellite Earth observation with UAV and in situ sensors so that deformation, surface composition and the shallow subsurface can be watched together.

That work is centred on **MOSMIN**, a Horizon Europe action for multiscale observation of mine operations. Copernicus supplies wide-area deformation and composition maps; drones and ground sensors, machine-learning fusion and distributed fibre-optic sensing fill the gaps at higher resolution. The same stack supports geotechnical and environmental monitoring and the valorisation of mining-related deposits.

The practical goals are lower safety and environmental risk, greener observation tools, and transparent ESG reporting — without waiting for the next field campaign.

projects.title: curlew neural field modelling
projects.body:
**curlew** is an open-source Python toolkit for 2- and 3-dimensional geological models built with neural fields. Diverse geological data can be included in a graph-based framework so that unconformities, folds, faults and intrusions are constructed in geological-history order.

The same framework also builds synthetic geology, replacing neural fields with simple mathematical functions that can be sampled for testing and algorithm development. Everything is implemented in a differentiable way with PyTorch, so the models can sit inside inversion and optimisation workflows.

Source and docs: [github.com/samthiele/curlew](https://github.com/samthiele/curlew). The method is described by Kamath, Thiele and others (2026), *Curlew 1.0: Spatio-temporal implicit geological modelling with neural fields in python*, [Solid Earth](https://doi.org/10.31223/X5KX81).

projects.title: hylite hyperspectral toolboxes
projects.body:
**hylite** is an open-source Python toolbox for loading and preprocessing imagery from a range of hyperspectral sensors, applying analyses such as multi-feature minimum-wavelength mapping, dimensionality reduction and band ratios, and fusing HSI with high-resolution point clouds into radiometrically corrected hyperclouds. Spectral libraries and ground or laboratory measurements can be integrated for supervised classification. The same methods apply across spectral data types — libraries, images and point clouds — so they can be analysed and combined in one workflow.

That cross-sensor, cross-modality design covers drill-core scanning and core-shed mosaics, UAV and satellite surveys (including oblique pushbroom geometry), outcrop and open-pit mapping, hyperclouds that attach spectra to 3-D geometry, and interactive work with spectral libraries. The same preprocessing, correction and visualisation tools therefore serve laboratory samples, field scenes and Earth-observation datasets.

hylite is the core of a wider open-source hyperspectral stack. Companion packages include [hycore](https://github.com/samthiele/hycore) and [hywiz](https://github.com/samthiele/hywiz) for organising and viewing drill-core libraries, [hklearn](https://github.com/samthiele/hklearn) for multi-sensor machine learning, [ispec](https://github.com/samthiele/ispec) for querying and mixing spectral libraries, [crunchy](https://github.com/samthiele/crunchy) for realtime multithreaded processing, and a developing [napari-hippo](https://github.com/samthiele/napari-hippo) interface.

Source and docs: [github.com/hifexplo/hylite](https://github.com/hifexplo/hylite), [hifexplo.github.io/hylite](https://hifexplo.github.io/hylite/hylite.html).

projects.body: Recycling and second use of automotive lights — efficient sensor solutions for sorting and for supporting disassembly control and automation.

projects.title: DigIT
projects.funding: BMFTR EGARoh — digitization and geomodelling for intelligent exploration
projects.body:
**DigIT** develops digital technologies for non-invasive, near-mine exploration of critical raw materials. Mining continually exposes geological information on pit walls and underground faces, but time and current methods mean most of it is lost. DigIT captures that information quickly and feeds it into deposit-scale exploration, so discoveries can sit next to active or historic mines where infrastructure already exists and social and environmental constraints are often easier to meet.

The work has four strands: safe, objective mapping of mining areas by combining digital outcrops with visible–SWIR and long-wave infrared hyperspectral imaging (including underground workflows); self-updating geological models that absorb new mine-face data; physical-chemical simulation of ore-forming processes to derive exploration targets; and data standards that keep mapping archives interoperable and reusable. HIF leads hyperspectral mapping, geometallurgical upscaling and neural-field 3-D models; Terranigma extends LiquidEarth for immersive mapping and real-time model updates.

The methods are demonstrated in the Sn–(Li)–W-rich Ore Mountains (Erzgebirge) and the Cu-rich Iberian Pyrite Belt. Project site: [digital-exploration.de](https://digital-exploration.de/).

projects.title: RESTORE
projects.body: European initiative focused on an integrated and scalable battery recycling process for end-of-life electric-vehicle and domestic batteries, including sensor-based in-line monitoring of black-mass beneficiation.

projects.title: RegioREC
projects.body: Recycling and second use of Li-ion batteries — development of sensor-based logistics for in-line battery identification and digitalisation.

projects.title: MOSMIN
projects.funding: HORIZON-EUSPA Innovation Action — Multiscale Observation of Operations in Mines
partners: Centre Tecnològic de Telecomunicacions de Catalunya (CTTC)
projects.body:
Holistic full-site services for geotechnical and environmental monitoring and valorisation of mining-related deposits, using Earth observation and in situ geophysics. Copernicus supports deformation and surface-composition mapping; UAV and in situ sensors, machine-learning fusion and resolution enhancement, and distributed fibre-optic sensing address the subsurface.

Goals include greener EO tools, lower environmental and safety risk, EU resilience via secondary critical raw materials, and ESG transparency. Project site: [mosmin.eu](https://www.mosmin.eu/).

projects.funding: BMWK — new automotive and system technologies
projects.body: Automated solutions for robust, real-time identification of car recycling products, with a focus on advanced type discrimination for steel and aluminium in complex material mixes using hyperspectral imaging and LIBS-based validation.

projects.title: FINEST — Finest Mineral Additives
projects.body: Development of optical sensor solutions for mineral additives in polymers used in building insulation material (ETICS).

projects.title: AutoTarget
projects.body:
Autonomous, task-distributed drone network for isolated remote targets. HIF leads drone design, spectral imaging and machine learning; KIT-IIIT contributes sensor fusion, navigation, communications and automated decisions; CASUS contributes machine learning and real-time anomaly detection.

Open software: [github.com/hifexplo/autotarget](https://github.com/hifexplo/autotarget).

projects.title: HyperUAV-1
projects.body:
UAVs bridge ground versus airborne and satellite hyperspectral imaging. This CASUS Open Project develops methods to integrate and extrapolate across scales for mineral exploration and ecological parameter estimation: characterise spectral variations from ground to satellite, quantify linear and non-linear mixing with ground-sample distance, and explore super-resolution and generative enhancement.

See also the project page [HyperUAV](https://www.iexplo.space/hyperuav).

![Cover](fig-01.png)

projects.title: HyperUAV-2
projects.body: Scaling hyperspectral data to meaningfully quantify essential ecosystem variables. The project uses methods from HyperUAV-1 to develop data-driven models that bridge ground, UAV and satellite-scale hyperspectral observations.

projects.title: VECTOR
partners: Foundation Institute for the Study of Change
projects.body: Horizon Europe project on social attitudes, environmental and technical challenges to mining in Europe, including hyperspectral drill-core scanning of Irish sedimentary basins.

projects.title: H2GIGA / ReNaRe-AI4H2
projects.funding: BMBF cluster project — recycling, sustainable resource use
projects.body: Development of an efficient sensor combination for the rapid characterisation of electrolyser cells, and digitalisation of material composition for subsequent recycling decisions.

projects.title: DIGISORT
projects.funding: BMBF cluster project — recycling / green batteries
projects.body: Digitisation of mechanical separation (for example wind sifting of shredded Li-ion batteries). HIF records on-line particle size, shape and material properties of input and product streams with a multi-sensor setup on a conveyor, and consolidates method-specific data in real time. The approach is intended to transfer beyond Li-ion recycling.

projects.title: InfraDatRec
projects.funding: BMBF infrastructure — Data Mining Lab Freiberg
projects.body: Improvement of data availability in the field of battery materials and technologies, including infrastructure for in-line sensing (XRF, LIBS, robots, conveyor, GPU).

projects.title: TheiaX
projects.body: TheiaX GmbH is a HIF/HZDR spin-off applying hyperspectral imaging and machine learning to exploration and mining. Incubation was via Helmholtz Enterprise, with early services through HZDR Innovation GmbH; the legal entity was founded in December 2021. Work includes tripod and drone HSI, drill-core HSI, and machine-learning data fusion.

projects.title: RAMSES-4-CE
projects.body:
The rapid identification of critical compounds is crucial for adequate sorting and the adapted recycling that will enable a circular economy. RAMSES-4-CE is a four-year upscaling project funded by EIT RawMaterials to bring latest research into technical solutions for the resource industry. The project innovates optical spectroscopy-based multi-sensor systems for the recycling industry.

We address this challenge by using a combination of imaging sensors to identify key chemical compounds in material streams. Hyperspectral (HSI) reflectance spectroscopy in the near- and mid-infrared can identify and classify certain alloys, ceramics, and plastics. Laser-induced fluorescence (LiF) spectroscopy enables the detection of rare-earth elements and low-reflective black plastics, among others. To increase the range of waste classes, we add a rapid, non-destructive Raman sensor, integrated into the existing LiF and HSI system developed during inSPECtor.

Data are processed and analysed immediately using machine learning, so that the fully integrated sensor network can operate in sequential component-mapping mode with immediate data fusion.

projects.title: inSPECtor
projects.body: Development of an integrated reflectance and laser-induced fluorescence sensor system for rare-earth element mapping in drill cores.

projects.title: Mulsedro
projects.funding: EIT RawMaterials upscaling project — multi-sensor drones for geology mapping
partners: Geological Survey of Denmark and Greenland (GEUS)
projects.body: Development of two drone systems equipped with photogrammetry, magnetic, and hyperspectral sensors for exploration, mining-activity monitoring and post-mining rehabilitation.

pages.title: Innovative Exploration
pages.lede: We develop new technologies and workflows for the fast, non-invasive and economic exploration of mineral resources.
pages.body: We work at the Helmholtz Institute Freiberg for Resource Technology (HZDR-HIF) on multisensor integration, real-time resource characterisation, and autonomous mapping platforms.
